introduction: CI answers whether an artifact passed checks. GitOps answers which approved artifact/configuration the cluster should run. Keep those responsibilities separate so a build job does not also need broad cluster administration.

You will install Argo CD, first reconcile a small podinfo reference Deployment, then manage the existing Taskboard Deployment/Service from a configuration repository. Existing Secrets and PostgreSQL are deliberately outside this application ownership boundary.
prerequisites: Ubuntu 24.04 Bash in WSL2 or a disposable Linux VM; Docker is running. Use the same terminal unless a step names a second terminal.

Weeks9–12 GitLab project and passing build/system pipeline; week29 persistent Taskboard. Have an empty dedicated GitLab configuration repository. For this bounded lab it may be publicly readable only if it contains no secrets, credentials or private organizational data; otherwise configure a read-only repository credential before proceeding.

concepts.title: Promotion is an identity chain
paragraphs: Record source commit → pipeline/test evidence → registry digest → configuration commit → deployed image identity. A tag can move; a digest identifies registry content. Review the environment change separately from building it.
The supplied CI pipeline exports tested-digest.txt only after system tests pass. Use that artifact, not a tag copied from a different build.
concepts.example: GitLab publishes registry/project@sha256:...; the environment commit changes only that image reference and reviewed configuration.
concepts.judgment: A controller faithfully applies malicious desired state too. Protected branches, review, least-privilege controller scope and credential handling remain necessary.

concepts.title: Sync, self-heal and pruning differ
paragraphs: Sync applies desired configuration. Self-heal repairs manual drift. Pruning deletes live objects removed from source. Begin with explicit synchronization and pruning off so removal semantics are visible.
Do not let both HPA and a GitOps desired replica field continuously overwrite the same value. Week30 removed the HPA before this exercise.
concepts.example: A manual scale to3 appears OutOfSync when Git says2; enabling self-heal can return it to2.
concepts.judgment: An emergency change must either update source or deliberately pause the controller with a recorded reason; otherwise reconciliation can undo mitigation.

steps.title: Install the reconciler
steps.purpose: Treat the controller as privileged platform software.

commands.code:
export KUBECONFIG="$HOME/dev-opps-lab/k8s/kubeconfig"
kubectl config current-context
cd "$HOME/dev-opps-lab/k8s"
ARGO_TAG=$(curl -fsSL https://api.github.com/repos/argoproj/argo-cd/releases/latest | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["tag_name"])')
curl -fL "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/argoproj/argo-cd/$ARGO_TAG/manifests/install.yaml" -o argocd-install.yaml
kubectl create namespace argocd
kubectl apply -n argocd -f argocd-install.yaml
kubectl -n argocd rollout status deployment/argocd-repo-server --timeout=240s
kubectl -n argocd rollout status statefulset/argocd-application-controller --timeout=240s
explain: Resolve one official release, save the exact installation manifest and review its cluster-wide privileges. Create an isolated controller namespace; wait for repository and reconciliation components. Nothing exposes the web interface publicly.
commands.expected: Repo server and application controller Ready.
commands.troubleshoot: If image pulls or resources fail, inspect argocd namespace events before adding applications.

steps.checkpoint: Record release tag and removal plan.

steps.title: Create the environment repository
steps.purpose: Start with podinfo, then add the known Taskboard manifests without Secrets.

commands.code:
read -r -p 'HTTPS clone URL of your empty configuration repository: ' CONFIG_REPO
mkdir -p "$HOME/dev-opps-lab/environments"
cd "$HOME/dev-opps-lab/environments"
git clone "$CONFIG_REPO" devopps
cd devopps
git switch -c main
mkdir -p env/devopps
kubectl create deployment platform-reference --image=ghcr.io/stefanprodan/podinfo:6.9.2 --port=9898 --dry-run=client -o yaml > env/devopps/podinfo.yaml
git add env/devopps/podinfo.yaml
git commit -m 'Declare a reference workload for reconciliation'
git push -u origin main
explain: read collects your real repository URL instead of inventing one. mkdir/cd give the clone an explicit local location; git clone retrieves repository metadata. The empty repository receives a main branch.

kubectl --dry-run=client writes a reference Deployment without creating it. git add stages only that manifest; commit records it; push publishes the configuration to your own configured remote. Use your existing GitLab authentication; never place an access token in the URL.
commands.expected: One reviewed reference manifest on main.
commands.troubleshoot: If the empty remote already has main, use git switch main instead of creating it again. If push is rejected, inspect branch permissions rather than bypassing protections.

explain: This unquoted heredoc substitutes only the collected repository URL. The AppProject limits source repository, destination namespace and resource kinds. The Application points at the reviewed directory; no automated or prune policy is enabled.

The operation.sync request asks Argo to apply the current desired revision. get -w watches status; stop with Ctrl+C after Synced/Healthy. A reachable private repository needs a read-only credential, not a broader destination project.
commands.troubleshoot: ComparisonError commonly indicates repository access/path; SyncFailed can indicate a project restriction or invalid manifest. Read status.conditions and operationState.message.

steps.checkpoint: Confirm platform-reference /healthz via kubectl port-forward deployment/platform-reference 19898:9898 --address=127.0.0.1 and curl http://127.0.0.1:19898/healthz.

steps.title: Promote the tested Taskboard artifact
steps.purpose: Add only Deployment/Service ownership; leave database and credentials separate.

explain: Copy the known Deployment and Service into the configuration repository. They contain Secret references, not credential values.
commands.expected: The two manifests exist before any credential reference is patched.
commands.troubleshoot: Stop on the first unexpected result. Compare the named environment and prerequisites before changing anything.

commands.code:
read -r -p 'Private registry hostname (for example registry.gitlab.com): ' REGISTRY
read -r -p 'Read-only deploy-token username: ' REGISTRY_USER
read -r -s -p 'Read-only deploy-token value: ' REGISTRY_TOKEN
printf '
'
kubectl -n devopps create secret docker-registry registry-read --docker-server="$REGISTRY" --docker-username="$REGISTRY_USER" --docker-password="$REGISTRY_TOKEN"
unset REGISTRY_TOKEN
kubectl patch --local -f env/devopps/taskboard.yaml --type=strategic -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"imagePullSecrets":[{"name":"registry-read"}]}}}}' -o yaml > env/devopps/taskboard-next.yaml
mv env/devopps/taskboard-next.yaml env/devopps/taskboard.yaml
explain: For the private GitLab registry used by this course, create the read-only pull Secret before the first rollout. -s hides terminal input and unset removes the shell variable after use.
The local manifest patch stores only the Secret name in Git. It does not deploy yet. For a deliberately public image, omit this whole credential block.
A local administrator can inspect command arguments; use only a scoped disposable read_registry token.
commands.expected: A registry-read Secret exists and the local Pod template references it before image promotion.
commands.troubleshoot: Stop on the first unexpected result. Compare the named environment and prerequisites before changing anything.

commands.code:
read -r -p 'Exact IMAGE_REF from successful system job tested-digest.txt: ' IMAGE_REF
case "$IMAGE_REF" in *@sha256:*) ;; *) echo 'A registry digest is required'; exit 1 ;; esac
kubectl set image --local -f env/devopps/taskboard.yaml app="$IMAGE_REF" -o yaml > env/devopps/taskboard-next.yaml
mv env/devopps/taskboard-next.yaml env/devopps/taskboard.yaml
git diff -- env/devopps
git add env/devopps/taskboard.yaml env/devopps/service.yaml
git commit -m 'Promote system-tested Taskboard digest'
git push
kubectl -n argocd patch application devopps --type=merge -p '{"operation":{"sync":{}}}'
kubectl -n devopps rollout status deployment/taskboard --timeout=180s
kubectl -n devopps get pods -l app=taskboard -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.containerStatuses[*].imageID}'
explain: Select the exact tested registry digest, update the local manifest, review the diff, commit and push. Argo then reconciles both the image and its pull-secret reference together.

rollout waits only after the image pull prerequisite exists. Read imageID to connect the running artifact with the tested digest; distinguish a multi-platform index from its selected platform manifest.
commands.expected: The private image pulls and the new Pods become Ready.
commands.troubleshoot: Stop on the first unexpected result. Compare the named environment and prerequisites before changing anything.

steps.checkpoint: Keep build pipeline URL, test report, artifact digest, environment commit and deployed identity in one release record.

failure.title: A manual change drifts from Git
failure.boundary: Only desired replicas; HPA must be absent.

inject.code:
kubectl -n devopps scale deployment/taskboard --replicas=3
kubectl -n argocd annotate application devopps argocd.argoproj.io/refresh=normal --overwrite
explain: Scale creates intentional drift; refresh asks Argo to compare sooner.
inject.expected: Application becomes OutOfSync; manual sync policy leaves3replicas.
inject.troubleshoot: Wait for comparison; absence of immediate status change does not prove no drift.

investigate.code:
kubectl -n argocd get application devopps -o yaml
kubectl -n devopps get deployment taskboard
explain: Compare sync status, observed revision and live replicas to Git.
investigate.troubleshoot: Check no HPA or second reconciler owns replicas.

explanation: The controller has detected a difference but manual sync does not automatically repair it. Explicit sync applies the reviewed source; optional self-heal changes that operating policy.

recover.troubleshoot: If Git itself says3, review the source commit before changing anything.

verification.code:
kubectl -n argocd get application devopps
kubectl -n devopps get deployment taskboard
explain: Check both convergence and workload health.
verification.troubleshoot: Synced alone does not prove business behavior; run system checks.

questions.answer: Review, protected refs, least-privilege projects and trusted credentials; the controller itself applies authorized source, including mistakes.

questions.prompt: Why keep SOPS ciphertext out until integration is understood?
questions.answer: A controller needs an explicitly configured and constrained decryption mechanism. Encrypting a file without that contract creates a failed deployment or unsafe key handling.

questions.prompt: Does reverting Git safely reverse a migration?
questions.answer: No. A previous app may not understand the new schema/data. Use backward-compatible migrations and a separate recovery decision.

exercise.brief: Document and test self-heal separately from pruning.
hints: spec.syncPolicy.automated supports selfHeal and prune independently.
solution: After recording manual behavior, enable automated:{enabled:true,selfHeal:true,prune:false} on the Application, repeat the replica change and observe repair. Restore manual policy for gate32 if you want explicit release approval.

explain: Keep explicit synchronization for the next gate. Stop any local port-forward with Ctrl+C; retain Argo and repository.
cleanup.troubleshoot: Do not delete the Application with a cascading finalizer unless you intentionally want its managed workloads removed.

repoConnections.application: Compare manual drift with explicit sync, then optional self-heal; keep database/Secrets outside this ownership boundary.
Prove repository/controller synchronization with podinfo before adding Taskboard credentials and storage dependencies.

notes: Argo/GitLab execution requires the learner cluster and repository. No repository was published or cloud resource created during authoring.
title: GitLab CI plus Argo CD
outcome: Separate building an artifact from reconciling a cluster to approved configuration.
